description:
Make the shipped pre-commit and pre-push hooks ask `jit claim status` whether an issue's lease is held, so they depend on no claims file layout.

## Background

The strict-mode lease checks in `scripts/hooks/pre-commit:94-102` and `scripts/hooks/pre-push:76-89` read `.git/jit/claims.index.json` with `jq` and test its stored `stale` field; pre-push matches the issue by prefix (`startswith`). The scripts are embedded through `include_str!` (`crates/jit/src/commands/hooks.rs:7-8`). Their tests (`commands/hooks.rs:284-325`) plant an index file by hand (`grant_lease`) and run the hook in a scratch git repository; they run inside the library's unit tests, where no built binary is on the path. `jit claim status --issue <id> --json` reports one issue's leases with `stale` computed at read time. The CLI suite `crates/jit/tests/cli_repo_workflow/` runs the built binary. Kept as one change for a test reason: once the hooks call `jit`, the in-crate hook tests cannot pass, so they move to the CLI suite with the hooks.

## Success Criteria

- [hard] REQ-01: The pre-commit and pre-push hooks decide lease ownership from `jit claim status --issue <id> --json` and read no file under `.git/jit/`.
- [hard] REQ-02: A held, non-stale lease of the committing agent allows the commit; no lease, another agent's lease or a stale lease blocks it.
- [hard] REQ-03: The hook lease tests run in the CLI suite against the built binary and acquire the lease through `jit claim acquire`; `commands/hooks.rs` holds no lease test and plants no claims file.

## Notes

- Written against the code as it stands after the semantic-types epic (2195c98f): issue ids are `IssueId`, gate-run ids `GateRunId`, gate keys `GateKey`, lease ids `LeaseId`, events are an `Event` envelope around a tagged `EventBody`, and record paths come from `VirtualPath` constructors. Line citations name current code, which that epic retypes.
title: Git hooks check leases through the claim status command
